*Last updated: September 2026*


Insight Enterprises started in 1988 as Hard Drives International, a mail-order computer storage business run by brothers Eric and Tim Crown out of Arizona. It is now a Fortune 500 solutions integrator trading on Nasdaq as NSIT, doing $8.25 billion in revenue across 19 countries. But the number that matters to a student is different. Insight publishes a complete internship specification rather than a marketing page: a named cohort program called Summer 360, 10 weeks, open to college sophomores, juniors and seniors, with three named training sessions built in, plus a separate 15-week co-op that runs in fall, spring and summer semesters. And it publishes named interns, with photographs and full interviews, describing how they converted. One of them, Cayla Millar, says the thing most students want to know: "The CEO, founders and senior leaders met with the interns; I thought it was awesome that Insight cared about their interns that much."

## What Is an Insight Enterprises Internship?


An Insight Enterprises internship is a paid, 10-week summer placement through the company’s Summer 360 cohort program, which puts college students into real roles across marketing, project management, web content, public-sector business analysis, HR and technical functions at a[Fortune 500 solutions integrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insight_Enterprises) with $8.25 billion in revenue and 15,000 employees across 19 countries. Founded in 1988 as Hard Drives International by Eric and Tim Crown, Insight now operates with deep expertise in cloud, data, AI, cybersecurity and intelligent edge. Beyond the summer track, Insight runs a 15-week co-op across fall, spring and summer semesters for students pursuing technical or IT-related degrees. Interns rate the culture highly: former intern Brock Jacobs says, "Even as an intern my perspective was always valued and taken into account. Everyone gives you a fair shot. You’re never treated as a temporary employee." The company holds a 3.5 out of 5 on Indeed from[606 reviews](https://www.indeed.com/cmp/Insight-596591c7/reviews) .


## When Do Insight Enterprises Internship Applications Open for 2027–2028?


Insight runs a well-documented Summer 360 internship and a separate co-op program, but it does not publish an application calendar. As of September 2026, all 150 open positions on Insight’s Eightfold job board have been checked and zero are intern or co-op requisitions. The prior cycle’s internship ran June 2 to August 8, 2025, which means postings for Summer 2027 should surface from late 2026 into spring 2027. Because co-ops run in fall, spring and summer semesters, co-op requisitions appear more frequently than internship ones, and a student who misses the summer window has two other legitimate shots each year.

### Why You Must Apply the Week Applications Open


Insight is a Fortune 500 employer that publishes a complete program specification and, unusually, opens its Summer 360 cohort to sophomores. That wider eligibility window means a larger applicant pool per seat, and the company’s Eightfold AI matching platform screens resumes before a human sees them. Applying the day postings go live, with a resume that mirrors the requisition’s own terminology, is the formula. Insight’s own published intern interviews show that conversion requires initiative, not just showing up: Cayla Millar stayed in touch with her manager, did a second internship, and applied when a full-time role opened. Brock Jacobs converted by volunteering for projects outside his assigned team. The message is clear: the cohort is small enough that individual effort is visible, and early entry gives you the longest runway to demonstrate it. And if you miss the summer window, the 15-week co-op runs three semesters a year.

## Which Insight Enterprises Internship Programs Should You Target?


Insight offers two distinct early-career tracks, both well-documented on the company’s own careers page. Which one to target depends on your major and whether you want a cohort summer experience or a longer, semester-aligned placement.


Program Focus Duration Key details


Summer 360 Internship Cohort-style placement across marketing, project management, web content, public-sector business analysis, HR and technical functions 10 weeks Paid; open to sophomores, juniors and seniors; hybrid or remote depending on program manager; three named training sessions


Co-op Extended hands-on experience applying classroom learning to real work in technical and IT-related disciplines 15 weeks Runs fall, spring and summer semesters; requires a technical or IT-related bachelor’s degree; hybrid or remote depending on program manager


See all openings at[careers.insight.com](https://careers.insight.com/careers) . The Summer 360 internship is the broader entry point (open to multiple majors and class years), while the co-op is deeper and more technical. Both lead to the same four published career destinations: Architect, Account Manager, Project Manager and Team Lead.


## What Are the Eligibility Requirements?


Insight publishes more eligibility detail than most Fortune 500 technology employers. Here is what the program page and the last recoverable requisition state:


• **Internship (Summer 360):** "College sophomores, juniors and seniors are eligible" — an unusually wide window. Most Fortune 500 tech internships gate at rising junior.


• **Co-op:** "Students pursuing a technical or IT-related bachelor’s degree are eligible."


• **Individual reqs may be stricter.** The Summer 2025 IPS Business Analyst Intern role required a "rising senior" with a major in Finance, Accounting, Marketing, Business Administration or Business Management.


• **Full-term attendance required.** The prior-cycle requisition listed the ability to attend the full 10-week term as a qualification, not a preference.


• **GPA:** not published. Neither the program page nor the recoverable requisition names a GPA cutoff.


• **Work authorization:** not established. Neither the program page nor the recoverable requisition contains a work-authorization or sponsorship clause.


### Does Insight Require a Specific Major?


Not at the program level. The Summer 360 cohort is open to sophomores, juniors and seniors across disciplines, and Insight’s published intern interviews include marketing, project management, web content and HR tracks. However, individual requisitions do specify majors: the IPS Business Analyst Intern required Finance, Accounting, Marketing, Business Administration or Business Management. And the co-op track explicitly requires a "technical or IT-related bachelor’s degree." Read each posting’s own qualification line rather than relying on the program-level statement.


## What Skills Does Insight Enterprises Look For, and How Do You Build Them?


Insight’s internship requisitions name activities, not tools, and the company’s program page promises to "develop additional technical skills and vital soft skills." The one fully recoverable intern JD (IPS Business Analyst Intern, Chandler AZ, Summer 2025) centers on CRM and BI analysis, KPI reporting, dashboard building and public-sector market research. Across the broader organization, Insight names five capability areas: cloud, data, AI, cybersecurity and intelligent edge. What matters most for a candidate is that Insight names no specific software in its intern requisitions. It asks for the activity (CRM/BI analysis, dashboards) rather than the tool, which means a candidate who arrives with a finished BI or market-research artifact is answering the requisition in its own terms.

## What Is the Insight Enterprises Application and Interview Process Like?


Insight does not publish an interview process for interns, but the application mechanics and one verified channel are documented:


1. **Save both searches at[careers.insight.com](https://careers.insight.com/careers) .** Use the pre-built internship filter (` ?query=Internship&location=United+States` ) and the co-op filter (` ?query=co-op&location=United+States` ). Both currently return zero results, which is the correct pre-open state.


2. **Apply through Eightfold.** careers.insight.com runs on Eightfold AI’s smartapply platform. Mirror the requisition’s exact vocabulary in your resume: "KPI reporting," "CRM/BI analysis," "dashboards," "channel management," "solution sales."


3. **Commit to the full 10-week term.** The prior-cycle requisition made full-term attendance an explicit qualification, not a preference.


4. **Go to the career fair.** Insight publishes its own guide, "Career Fair Tips: How to Stand Out & Get the Job," signaling that campus fairs are a real recruiting channel.


5. **Use a referral if you have one.** Cayla Millar applied after a friend at Insight suggested she was a cultural fit and used that friend as a reference.


Interview stages are not published. With no live postings until at least late 2026, the actionable move now is to save both searches and attend any career fair where Insight appears this fall.

## How Do You Stand Out at a Fortune 500 Solutions Integrator?


Three moves, all executable before the window opens. First, learn what "channel" means. Insight is a solutions integrator: it resells, integrates and services technology from Microsoft, Google Cloud and hundreds of other vendors. The intern requisition asks for "knowledge in channel management and solution sales." Being able to explain why a company buys through Insight rather than direct puts you ahead of most applicants who have never heard the term. Second, name one of Insight’s five capability areas and have a real opinion about it: cloud, data, AI, cybersecurity or intelligent edge. Third, evidence the values. Hunger, Heart and Harmony are not decoration here. Every one of Insight’s four published former interns references them unprompted, and Brock Jacobs attributes his conversion specifically to volunteering for projects outside his assigned team. Arrive with one concrete story for each value, and be ready to say the words. A finished Externship project in BI, channel strategy or market research gives you a fourth move: the concrete artifact that turns "interested in IT solutions" into a demonstrated capability.

## FAQ


### Can I still apply for a summer 2026 Insight Enterprises internship?


No. The Summer 2026 cycle has ended. The prior cycle’s internship ran June 2 to August 8, 2025, and those postings are long closed. The next window is Summer 2027: watch careers.insight.com from late 2026 into spring 2027, and check both the internship and co-op filters.


### What is the Insight Summer 360 program?


Summer 360 is Insight’s named cohort internship: a 10-week summer placement described on the company’s own early-career programs page as "a unique opportunity to meet other students and participate in a cohort-style internship." It includes three training sessions: Presentation Advantage, Wealth and Financial Independence, and a Professional Image Workshop. Open to college sophomores, juniors and seniors.


### Can sophomores apply to Insight internships?


Yes at the program level. The early-career programs page says "College sophomores, juniors and seniors are eligible," which is more open than most Fortune 500 technology internships. Individual requisitions may narrow it: the Summer 2025 IPS Business Analyst Intern role required a rising senior. Read each posting’s own class-year line.


### How much do Insight Enterprises interns get paid?


No figure is published. Insight’s program page says "competitive compensation," and the one recoverable intern requisition carried no pay range. Indeed has no Insight intern salary data. Check the live requisition when postings appear.


### What is the difference between an Insight internship and a co-op?


The internship is the 10-week Summer 360 cohort program, open to sophomores through seniors across disciplines. The co-op is a 15-week program that runs in fall, spring and summer semesters, limited to students pursuing a technical or IT-related bachelor’s degree. The co-op gives you three chances a year rather than one.


### Does Insight hire its interns full-time?


Insight publishes no conversion rate, but it publishes something unusual: a full interview series with named former interns describing exactly how they converted. None received an automatic return offer. Cayla Millar stayed in touch with her manager, did a second internship, and applied when a role opened. Brock Jacobs converted by volunteering for projects outside his assigned team.


### Is Insight Enterprises the same as Insight Global?


No. Insight Enterprises (Nasdaq: NSIT) is a Fortune 500 IT solutions integrator headquartered in the Phoenix metro, founded in 1988 as Hard Drives International. Insight Global is a separate staffing company with its own, unrelated internship program. Search results mix them constantly.


### Are Insight internships remote or on-site?


It depends on the team. Insight’s program page says internships and co-ops "take place both in-person and online, depending on your program manager," and the recoverable requisition was posted as "a hybrid opportunity." An Insight internship may not require relocating to Arizona, but that is not guaranteed. Check the specific posting.


No Insight internship or co-op requisitions are live yet, and the window will not open until late 2026 at the earliest. Use the lead time: a[remote Externship](https://www.extern.com/externships) in BI, channel strategy or market research turns "interested in IT solutions" into a finished project an application can point at.
